title: Finite etale pushforward preserves constructible module sheaves
statement: Let $h:V\to U$ be a finite etale morphism [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category] of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and $G$ a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $V_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Then $h_*G$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is constructible on $U_{\Et}$ in the same finite constructible-stratification sense.

source.place: Tag 095H, label lemma-pushforward-constructible, module clause for finite coefficient rings

proof.text: Put $F=h_*G$. By [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-qcqs-affine-local] it suffices to show that $F$ is constructible on every affine open $A\subseteq U$. We will use inverse image and restriction interchangeably along etale maps: [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] gives the identification on underlying abelian sheaves, and [lemma-weil-pbc-etale-pullback-forget-modules] identifies the underlying abelian inverse image of a module sheaf. This identification is $\Lambda$-linear: for each $\lambda\in\Lambda$, naturality with respect to the abelian sheaf endomorphism $m\mapsto\lambda m$ gives $\rho(\lambda m)=\lambda\rho(m)$. Local sections of the constant ring are etale locally constant scalars, so the same equality holds for all sections of $\Lambda_T$. Thus these identifications are isomorphisms of module sheaves, not a change of coefficient category.

For each point $a\in A$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split] to $h$ at $a\in U$. Pull the resulting etale neighbourhood back to $A$; [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] makes it etale over $A$, and the specified point still lies above $a$. The decomposition into copies of the neighbourhood pulls back to the same finite number of copies, by the fibre-product universal property. These neighbourhoods cover $A$. The affine scheme $A$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply the covering-refinement clause of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-qcqs-cofinal-finite-coverings] to obtain a finite etale covering $q_b:B_b\to A$ with each $B_b$ affine and factoring through one such neighbourhood. Pull back the splitting once more. Thus $V\times_U B_b$ is a finite disjoint union of copies of $B_b$, with sheet maps $s_{bj}:B_b\to V\times_U B_b$. Form $B=\coprod_b B_b$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Its map $q:B\to A$ is surjective. It is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source], since its restriction to each open component is the etale map $q_b$. It is quasi-compact because it is a finite union of quasi-compact affine components, and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion], clause (2): the component affine opens have intersections $B_b$ when the indices agree and the empty scheme otherwise, all quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Hence $B$ and $A$ meet the qcqs hypotheses of constructibility descent. The finite sheet number is allowed to depend on $b$; no constant rank on the whole base is assumed.

source.place: Tag 04HN, label lemma-finite-etale-etale-local; literature/stacks-project/topologies.tex Tag 0218, label lemma-etale-affine

proof.text: For fixed $b$, put $V_b=V\times_U B_b$, $h_b:V_b\to B_b$, and $G_b=G|_{V_b}$. The projection $V_b\to V$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], applied to the etale composite $B_b\to A\to U$; the open immersion $A\to U$ and this composite are etale by clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Each sheet map is an open immersion, so its composite $B_b\to V_b\to V$ is etale by the same clauses. Thus all restrictions used in this step are defined on the small etale sites and are identified with module inverse images by step 1. The restriction of $F$ to $B_b$ is canonically $h_{b*}G_b$. Indeed, on an etale object $W\to B_b$, the two sides have sections $G(W\times_U V)$ and $G(W\times_{B_b}(B_b\times_U V))$ by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The isomorphism of fibre products is $(w,v)\mapsto(w,(q_b(w),v))$, with inverse $(w,(b,v))\mapsto(w,v)$. These maps commute with every $W\to W_1$ over $B_b$, so they induce inverse sheaf morphisms. They preserve scalar multiplication because the scalar section on each fibre product is the pullback of the same section on $W$. This is the restriction identification of step 1, applied in the module category. By [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-split-cover-product], $h_{b*}G_b\cong\prod_j G_b|_{s_{bj}}$. Each factor is the restriction of $G$ along the composite sheet map $B_b\to V$. It is constructible by [prop-constructible-pullback], read in $\mathrm{ModuleCat}(\Lambda)$; [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison] identifies its predicate with the finite-module-stratum predicate used here.

A finite product of these constructible module sheaves is constructible by an explicit induction using [thm-constructible-serre], clause (2). The product with no factors is the zero sheaf, constant with finite value $0$ on the single stratum $B_b$. If $P$ is the product of the first $r$ factors and $H$ the next factor, the sectionwise sequence $0\to P\to P\times H\to H\to0$, with maps $p\mapsto(p,0)$ and $(p,t)\mapsto t$, is split exact: its splitting is $t\mapsto(0,t)$ and its kernel is exactly $P\times\{0\}$. Clause (2) therefore makes $P\times H$ constructible. This proves the induction for any finite number of factors. Transport the resulting stratum witnesses through the module isomorphisms in step 3; their pullbacks remain isomorphic to the same finite constant modules. Consequently $F|_{B_b}$ is constructible for every $b$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-qcqs-affine-local], the open cover of $B$ by its finitely many components $B_b$ shows that $q^{-1}(F|_A)$ is constructible. Here its restriction to $B_b$ is $F|_{B_b}$ by step 1, so step 4 provides the local witnesses. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-surjective-pullback] to the surjective morphism $q:B\to A$: both schemes are qcqs by step 2 and the coefficient ring is the given finite commutative ring. It follows that $F|_A$ is constructible. Since this holds for every affine open $A\subseteq U$, the affine-local criterion of step 1 makes $F=h_*G$ constructible on $U$ in precisely the stated global finite-stratification sense.
